passage: On the fourth-floor bay of the software firm, Shreya walked Himani over to Rishi's desk. "Himani, you know this codebase, and you never make anyone feel silly for asking. Could you pair with Rishi on Tuesdays and Thursdays?" Himani smiled. "Sure. Mornings?" Rishi looked relieved and a little shy. On the first Tuesday, Himani typed while Rishi watched, and then they switched. Himani showed how the team names branches, where the test folder lives, and which reviewer answers fastest. By the third week, Rishi had stopped sending Shreya the same three questions. Shreya's afternoons were quieter, and Rishi's tasks came in on time.

qa.q: On which days do Himani and Rishi pair?
qa.a: They pair on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

qa.q: How did Rishi feel when Himani agreed to pair?
qa.a: Rishi felt relieved and a little shy.

qa.q: What else could Shreya do to help the pairing work, and why?
qa.a: Shreya could check in with both after a month, because the pair may need to change the days or the topics as Rishi grows more confident.

qa.q: How might Himani feel about taking on the buddy role?
qa.a: Himani probably feels trusted and pleased to help, though it takes time out of Himani's own work.

grounding: Illustrates a lead assigning a friendly mid-level colleague to pair with a junior twice a week so the junior learns team habits faster and fewer explanations fall to the lead.
